_comment: What the platform must say about this repository, with why. Held by posture.yml (weekly, and on every push to main) with an administrator's token; setting_problems/unreadable/check_problems decide. A switch with no why is one the next person turns off to make something else work. The list of switches and what each wants is copied into tests/test_posture.py, so turning or removing one is red until the same pull request changes both.

enforce_admins.why: an exemption for admins is an exemption for anyone

required_linear_history.why: rebase only - a merge commit's message is nobody's

allow_force_pushes.why: history on main is what the DOIs point at

allow_deletions.why: the branch every consumer pins from

required_conversation_resolution.why: a review comment left open is a decision left open

strict_status_checks.why: linear history already implies the rebase a strict flag would demand (DECISIONS.md: strict-checks-off)

required_approving_review_count.why: honest rather than aspirational: a single maintainer cannot review their own work

allow_squash_merge.why: squash rewrites the subject past the 72-character gate and merges commits the gate judged one by one Not returned to a fine-grained token even with Administration:read and Contents:read (measured 2026-08-29), so it is printed with its declared value on every run for a person to check; the maintainer's session reads it and judges it.

allow_merge_commit.why: linear history is required - a merge commit could never land; the button should not offer it Not returned to a fine-grained token even with Administration:read and Contents:read (measured 2026-08-29), so it is printed with its declared value on every run for a person to check; the maintainer's session reads it and judges it.

allow_rebase_merge.why: the one merge shape linear history allows Not returned to a fine-grained token even with Administration:read and Contents:read (measured 2026-08-29), so it is printed with its declared value on every run for a person to check; the maintainer's session reads it and judges it.

delete_branch_on_merge.why: merged branches pile up unseen Not returned to a fine-grained token even with Administration:read and Contents:read (measured 2026-08-29), so it is printed with its declared value on every run for a person to check; the maintainer's session reads it and judges it.

web_commit_signoff_required.why: a commit made in the web editor must carry the same DCO sign-off as one made with git commit -s

sha_pinning_required.why: the rule's own incident (platform-posture-verified) found this off while SHA pinning was enforced only by our test; the platform refusing an unpinned action is the second lock, and it was off here until 2026-08-30

allowed_actions.why: every action this repository uses is GitHub's own (actions/*, github/*) or named one by one under selected_actions; a policy of 'all' lets the next workflow pull anyone's — 'selected' with GitHub-owned allowed and the named few is the smallest set that runs what runs today

dependabot_alerts.why: the advisories job audits the pins on every run, but only when a run happens; the platform's alerts are the watcher that works while nobody pushes (re-audit round 10: Dependabot had no receiver)

required_signatures.why: commits are not GPG/SSH-signed here; authorship is the DCO sign-off, held by commit-lint and web_commit_signoff_required, and requiring signatures would refuse the maintainer's own rebase merges — DECISIONS.md: git-signing-not-required. Declared so the switch cannot be flipped on by a click and start refusing merges unexplained

selected_actions.why: the detail behind 'selected': GitHub's own actions, nothing verified-by-marketplace, and one pattern naming one action — pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish, the trusted-publishing step of release.yml. The policy refused it at startup on 2026-09-05 (run 33937392727: not allowed because all actions must be from a repository owned by sayam or created by GitHub) while every check was green, because nothing read this register against the workflows' uses: lines — tests/test_instruments_dogfood.py does now, both ways. A pattern '*' under 'selected' is 'all' with a different word (pre-cut review, 2026-08-30); a pattern naming one action keeps the SHA pin the platform requires

not_required.release-sign: runs only when a release is published, never on a pull request; the release page shows it, and the maintainer sees it within 1 day
not_required.posture: runs weekly and on every push to main with the administrator's token, never on a pull request (bots' pull requests get no secrets); it also carries the schedule census and the DECISIONS revisit check, so those two clocks tick on the platform's cron rather than only on a push; its run page is the record, and the maintainer sees a red within 7 days
